entities.name: PMID:27493887
observations: Retrospective FNAC series of 4,849 unselected thyroid-nodule patients; BMI was categorized from normal weight through grade-3 obesity.
Thy4/Thy5 cytology prevalence was 6.8%, 6.3%, 6.3%, 4.0%, and 4.2% across increasing BMI categories (p=0.29); authors found no obesity association with differentiated thyroid carcinoma risk.
In grade-2/3 obese women, Thy4/Thy5 cytology was lower (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.284–0.920, p=0.009). Abstract does not report a formal interaction test or confirmed histologic-cancer endpoint.

entities.name: PMID:35222281
observations: Prospective cohort of 1,259 thyroid-nodule evaluations found no BMI association with cancer: mean BMI 28.9 versus 28.6 kg/m² in cancer versus benign disease, p=0.58; OR 1.007, 95% CI 0.98–1.03.
BMI did not predict aggressive thyroid cancer (p=0.15).

entities.name: PMID:37763777
observations: Retrospective AUS/FLUS cohort of 113 patients found no obesity association with malignancy; adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.93–1.06, p=0.87.

entities.name: PMID:24555500
observations: Pooled case-control analysis reported higher papillary thyroid cancer odds for overweight and obesity versus normal BMI: OR 1.72 and 4.17, respectively.
This broader epidemiologic evidence differs from cytology-selected nodule cohorts.

entities.name: Obesity-DTC cytology null
observations: In a cytology-selected thyroid-nodule series, increasing BMI did not increase suspicious or malignant Thy4/Thy5 cytology; evidence does not support obesity as a risk modifier in this setting.
